key_insight: Concentrating NACA0006 airfoil-grid rings near the pipe wall can suppress turbulence enough to produce net drag reduction, increasing flow rate by up to 9.0%.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical passive flow-control strategy for pipe networks that could lower pumping energy in water and gas transport if the added device losses stay small.
method: Axisymmetric RANS simulation with the k-ω SST turbulence model
Periodic boundary conditions to evaluate fully developed pipe flow
Validated against turbulent pipe flow and prior large-eddy breakup device experiments
evidence_signal: At a pressure difference corresponding to Re ≈ 10^5, the near-wall grid pattern increased flow rate by up to 9.0% and reduced area-integrated Reynolds shear stress by 29%.
watch_item: The result is model-based, so real-world performance may depend on fabrication tolerance, installation losses, and sensitivity to off-design Reynolds numbers.
paper_title: Net drag reduction in turbulent pipe flow by airfoil-section grids concentrated near the wall
